brief: Two constants on the punt have never been priced. First: since #141 gave it a second hull, WIND is its TOP refusal - windF >= 0.5 deletes 32.9% of genuine offers, roughly a third of the crossings - and nobody has swept that threshold against what a punt in this river can actually do. Second: the give-way rule between the swans and the hulls only clears a LANDING, so a swan gets to 1.05 cells of a hull under way. Instrument puntFits CLAUSE BY CLAUSE in its own evaluation order (the loudest refusal is usually the cheap boolean in front of the arithmetic), sweep the wind threshold, and make the give-way clear the whole TRACK rather than the landing point.
successLooksLike: Crossings per day rise on windy days with no stranding and no claim clash; swept end to end, the least swan-to-hull separation is at least the clearance the landing rule already promises; probes/punt.mjs still exits 0 on HEAD and 1 under --strand and --strand-late.
avoid: A threshold is not a share at small n: rank the days by their own hash and cut at the quantiles rather than tuning a constant against two seeds. Two movers on a track share a CORRIDOR, not a point - sweep whole paths, and if you offset, offset BOTH ends equally so the lanes stay parallel (this is exactly what #141 had to learn). #149 redefined punt.mjs's subject once already: if you change what a stranding IS, re-run every gate that reads it, not only the one you edited.
